title: Distinguish check, inspection and exploration
when: When the expected outcome requires assertions, visual judgment or exploratory observation.
need: Command/CI and Browser check use automatic results; Browser inspection captures evidence for agent judgment. Pack-added methods and exploratory missions have additional contracts. A screenshot is not a pass. Exploratory missions use informed_subagent from the controller; fresh targets stay free of a source checkout. Unsupported executors require a saved-case correction and rematerialization. When a deployment member is removed mid-walk, its original session still runs walk-end for teardown on the recorded host; it must retry a busy host and confirm scratch removal and starting-state restore without reopening the execution. A terminal deployment run also preserves the original session’s walk-end cleanup on the recorded host; cleanup settles a pending abort and records the run status. Mission reports include every host/setup workaround with evidence. The main reviewer must not pass a case when a workaround touched its tested behavior; rerun without that substitution. Real password, 2FA and payment steps stop the walker for a human handoff. During informed mission work the execution reads walking; after every host mission records walk-end it reads awaiting_walk_review; controller missions need no walk-end, lease or reset debt. A pending bundle is dispatch authority, not evidence that the walker has handed back. Authors split missions by machine for parallel host queues, with small cross-machine missions ordered last. Owners keep leases/verdicts and start fresh walkers per source case or small same-host group with compact host/window/fact/evidence handoffs, never large resumed histories. Host commands wait foreground with tool yield at least their timeout, never short-yield polling.
surface: Method definitions; Browser reference; exploratory QA dispatch
gap: Review question: should verification planning offer the relevant method in plain language and fetch its reference only after selection?
